title: Laboratory identification of the dark-matter particle

concept.text: The innovation would be a positive, independently replicated laboratory detection that identifies a particle or field as a constituent of galactic dark matter and constrains its mass and interaction with ordinary matter. The central achievement would connect a cosmological matter component to a specific physical species. Detecting one constituent would not, by itself, establish that it accounts for all dark matter.

Two search approaches illustrate what such identification could involve: measuring nuclear recoils caused by dark-matter scattering, as pursued by LZ, or detecting axion conversion power, as pursued by ADMX. A convincing signal would need a consistent physical interpretation and evidence distinguishing it from backgrounds. The supplied LZ and ADMX results document searches and exclusions, rather than identification of a dark-matter constituent.

Conceptual scope: WIMPs and axions are candidate routes to this discovery, rather than an exhaustive definition of the target. Another species could fulfill the concept if its connection to galactic dark matter were established. A laboratory signal alone need not uniquely determine mass, coupling strength and local abundance; the identification must state which properties are measured and which depend on assumptions.

significance.text: In the Planck 2018 base-ΛCDM fit, the cold-dark-matter density is Ω_c h² = 0.120 ± 0.001, compared with a baryon density of Ω_b h² = 0.0224 ± 0.0001. Their ratio is approximately 5.36, or about 5.4. Thus, within this cosmological model, the dark-matter component outweighs ordinary baryonic matter by more than five to one. These are cosmological density inferences, not measurements of a particle's identity.

Scientific significance, as a conditional assessment: identifying a species shown to constitute galactic dark matter would connect this large cosmological component to laboratory physics. Its inferred mass and interactions would give other experiments concrete targets for replication and complementary measurements. The advance would turn searches over candidate models into investigations of a particular constituent, providing a new basis for testing its role in cosmic structure.

The consequences would have important boundaries. Identification alone would not determine the species' production history, prove that it supplies all dark matter, or settle every ingredient of structure-formation cosmology. Technological applications would require additional capabilities beyond detection, and a revision of gravity would be a separate scientific claim. These are limits on the proposed discovery's implications, rather than reasons to diminish its significance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is to extract a reproducible dark-matter signal with enough distinguishing information to identify its source. LZ illustrates a concrete background problem: boron-8 solar neutrinos produce nuclear recoils in xenon with a spectrum resembling that of a roughly 5.5 GeV/c² dark-matter candidate. A low-energy recoil excess therefore requires careful statistical and physical discrimination before it can support a dark-matter interpretation.

Axion searches face a different coverage problem. The supplied ADMX result reaches the DFSZ benchmark over 3.27–3.34 μeV under specified halo and abundance assumptions. Sensitivity over that interval does not establish sensitivity at other masses or interactions. Extending the search requires maintaining the relevant detection sensitivity across additional parameter ranges; the supplied evidence does not quantify the fraction of all viable axion models already tested.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: the broader challenge combines sensitivity to weak signals, control of instrumental and physical backgrounds, reliable calibration, and independent measurements that can separate competing interpretations. Replication must test a shared particle hypothesis rather than merely reproduce an unexplained excess. Joint analyses also need to expose degeneracies among mass, interaction strength and local abundance, because multiple detections can retain common assumptions.

Open possibilities remain that the relevant interaction is weaker than the sensitivities documented here, or that the constituent lies outside the WIMP and axion models represented in these searches. These are possibilities, not conclusions established by the supplied experiments. Their null results constrain particular hypotheses and ranges; they do not establish comprehensive coverage of all candidates or the capabilities of every current detector.

current_state.text: LZ analyzed a 5.7 tonne-year exposure collected from March 2023 to April 2025. The supplied review identifies the result as published in Physical Review Letters 137, 091806 in 2026. It reports no significant excess attributable to dark-matter nuclear recoils in its 3–9 GeV/c² search and reports leading spin-independent limits down to 5 GeV/c². The review had a complete text extraction for this paper, so these numerical statements are supported by more than its metadata or abstract alone. The result constrains interactions in the analyzed range; it does not identify a dark-matter particle.

The same LZ analysis reports 4.5σ evidence for boron-8 solar coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering under the assumption of zero dark-matter events. That qualification matters: the significance describes the neutrino interpretation in that scenario, rather than a dark-matter discovery or an assumption-free separation of neutrinos from dark matter. The spectral resemblance to light-WIMP recoils explains why improving sensitivity also makes background discrimination more consequential.

The supplied 2025 ADMX abstract reports a 90% confidence exclusion of DFSZ axions with masses from 3.27 to 3.34 μeV. Its interpretation assumes a standard halo model and a local density of 0.45 GeV/cm³ consisting entirely of axions. This is a documented interval from one study, not an inventory of all ADMX exclusions. The review's access was limited to the abstract-level record, so the result is retained within that scope.

The earlier research attributes a 3.1 tonne-year exposure and no significant WIMP excess to a XENONnT result published on 24 November 2025. However, the supplied source index contains no captured text for its cited APS page, and the review could not verify those numbers or the attributed quotation. They remain reported claims from the research input, rather than established results in this record. The absence of captured evidence does not show that the result is false.

The earlier research also describes a later ADMX run at 1.10–1.31 GHz as reaching KSVZ sensitivity but not DFSZ sensitivity. No supplied source text documents that run, so its frequency range, relative chronology and benchmark sensitivity remain unverified here. Neither this claim nor the documented 3.27–3.34 μeV result supports saying that ADMX has excluded DFSZ axions only in that single interval.

Planck supplies a complementary cosmological result: a constrained cold-dark-matter density within base-ΛCDM, rather than a constituent identification. The review had the relevant abstract values and density passages. Its PDF extraction was truncated and skipped some form content, but the density text used for the numerical comparison was present. That access limitation does not invalidate the quoted parameter values, while it limits claims about material beyond the retained passages.

Coverage limitation: the supplied dated results do not identify a dark-matter constituent, but the research and review do not establish a comprehensive field-wide status as of 1 November 2026. The bounded freshness-search record is empty. Accordingly, this record preserves the documented results without treating them as proof that every identification route remains open or that no other relevant result exists.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: two independent experiments using different targets or methods report discovery-level signals consistent with a common particle mass and interaction model. Their spectra, modulation, directional information or conversion power should jointly distinguish that interpretation from known backgrounds, with quantified statistical and systematic uncertainties. This is a proposed evidentiary benchmark for this concept, not an established consensus standard or a prescription endorsed by the supplied papers.
completion_criteria.label: Independent experiments discover signals supporting common mass and interaction model

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirements: each collaboration should make its calibration, background treatment, uncertainty estimates and signal-model assumptions sufficiently available for independent scrutiny and repeat analysis. Follow-up measurements should test predictions beyond the feature that first produced the excess. Agreement across finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth over the conditions examined; it would not establish that a model applies universally.
completion_criteria.label: Enable independent repeat analysis and test further signal-model predictions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed astrophysical consistency requirement: the combined interpretation should be compatible with independently estimated galactic dark-matter density and should explicitly state the detected species' assumed abundance. Density–coupling degeneracies must be quantified or constrained with complementary information. Compatibility with the total density is a consistency check, not proof that the detected species supplies all of it; that stronger conclusion would require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Quantify density–coupling degeneracies and establish galactic density compatibility

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: the completed claim should specify the mass range, interaction channels, detector conditions and astrophysical assumptions actually tested. A tighter exclusion curve, an isolated excess below discovery significance, or a replicated instrumental effect would not meet the identification goal. Uncertainty in production history or the existence of additional dark components could remain after a convincing identification of one constituent.
completion_criteria.label: Specify experimental and astrophysical boundaries of the identification claim

related_concepts.text: Conceptual relationship to PHY-12, Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale: a species discovered as dark matter could also belong to a mechanism relevant to Higgs-mass protection, such as an appropriate supersymmetric model. That would create an overlap only if both roles were demonstrated. Establishing a galactic dark-matter constituent does not establish a Higgs-protecting mechanism, and establishing such a mechanism does not establish which species populates the galactic halo. The supplied sources do not demonstrate this connection.

Conceptual relationships to PHY-05, A tested microphysical account of the dark-energy scale, and PHY-13, A tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess: all connect microscopic physics with cosmological observations, but they answer different questions. PHY-04 concerns the identity of a dark-matter constituent; PHY-05 concerns the dark-energy scale; PHY-13 concerns the origin of the matter excess. A dark-matter identification could inform broader cosmological models without completing either neighboring concept or determining its own production history.

Conceptual relationships to PHY-03, A laboratory proof that gravity is non-classical, and PHY-11, A tested resolution of the black-hole information paradox: all could constrain fundamental descriptions of nature, but their evidentiary targets remain distinct. A dark-matter signal would require evidence connecting a detected species to the galactic matter component. It would not by itself establish non-classical gravity, resolve black-hole information, or require a revision of gravity.

Conceptual relationships to PHY-06, Discovery of a magnetic monopole; PHY-07, Observation of baryon-number violation; and PHY-08, Observation of lepton-number violation: these are separate discovery targets. A broader theory might connect one of them to dark matter, but the supplied material establishes no such connection. Each would require its own characteristic observation rather than follow automatically from identifying a dark-matter constituent.

Roster distinction: PHY-01, Ambient-pressure superconducting conductors at room temperature; PHY-02, Sustained net-electric power from controlled fusion; PHY-09, A coherent gamma-ray source; and PHY-10, Collider-quality plasma wakefield acceleration concern different material, energy or experimental capabilities. The supplied material documents no specific dependency or demonstrated overlap with PHY-04. They remain separate innovations.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish comprehensive dark-matter identification status as of 1 November 2026; no bounded freshness-search results were supplied.
The XENONnT 3.1 tonne-year exposure, publication details and reported null result lack captured source text in this record.
The later ADMX 1.10–1.31 GHz run, its chronology and its KSVZ-versus-DFSZ sensitivity lack supporting source text.
The total coverage of ADMX, other haloscopes and WIMP searches cannot be inferred from the documented studies, and no quantitative measure of the remaining parameter space is supplied.
Whether any future detected species supplies all or only part of dark matter, and how abundance–coupling degeneracies could be resolved, remain scientific questions.
No supplied evidence establishes a connection between a dark-matter constituent and the Higgs-mass mechanism in PHY-12.

brief.title: Identifying what dark matter is made of
possible: Scientists could identify a particle or field that makes up some of the Galaxy’s dark matter. Independent laboratory experiments would detect it, constrain its mass and measure how it interacts with ordinary matter.
why: In Planck’s standard model of the Universe, dark matter outweighs ordinary matter by more than five to one. Identifying a constituent would connect this large cosmic component to something scientists can study in a laboratory.

Researchers could investigate a particular constituent instead of searching among possible candidates. Its measured properties would give other experiments concrete targets and help scientists test its role in how cosmic structures form.

sources.showed: Planck inferred the cosmic densities of dark and ordinary matter within a standard model of the Universe. Dark matter outweighed ordinary matter by more than five to one.
sources.quote: We ﬁnd no compelling evidence for extensions to the base-ΛCDM model.
sources.cited_for: Dark matter represents a large share of cosmic matter within Planck’s cosmological model.
sources.not_established: A cosmic density estimate does not identify the particle or field responsible.

sources.showed: LZ found no significant dark-matter signal from recoiling atomic nuclei. It found evidence for solar neutrinos, particles from the Sun, assuming no dark-matter events.
sources.quote:
In the no-
dark-matter scenario, we observe a signal consistent with 8B CE νNS events, corresponding to a
4.5σ statistical significance.
sources.cited_for: Solar neutrinos can produce signals resembling those expected from light dark-matter particles.
sources.not_established: The experiment did not identify a dark-matter constituent or demonstrate its independent replication.

sources.showed: This is a laboratory search for weakly interacting massive particles, a proposed kind of dark matter.
sources.cited_for: It represents another laboratory search for a possible dark-matter constituent.
sources.not_established: A search without a significant excess does not identify a dark-matter constituent.

sources.showed: ADMX excluded a proposed axion model over a narrow mass interval. Axions are hypothetical particles; the result assumes they supply all local dark matter and follow a specified galactic distribution.
sources.quote: Sub-Kelvin noise temperatures are reached with an ultralow noise Josephson parametric amplifier cooled by a dilution refrigerator.
sources.cited_for: Axion searches can reach the sensitivity needed to test particular models over limited mass intervals.
sources.not_established: Excluding a model over a narrow interval neither detects axions nor rules them out at other masses.

shown: LZ has constrained how strongly light dark-matter candidates could interact with ordinary matter. ADMX has ruled out a particular axion model over a narrow mass interval under stated galactic assumptions. Neither result identifies a dark-matter constituent.
missing: A reproducible signal must distinguish dark matter from solar neutrinos, instrumental effects and other competing explanations.
Independent experiments must support the same mass and interaction model, then confirm further predictions.
Measurements must separate the effects of particle abundance and interaction strength, or state how assumptions link them.

milestones.label: Independent discoveries agree on the same particle
milestones.explanation: Independent experiments using different targets or methods would have to find discovery-level signals supporting a common mass and interaction model. Agreement would help distinguish dark matter from other signal sources.

milestones.label: Independent analysis and further predictions hold up
milestones.explanation: Calibration, background estimates and assumptions would have to support independent repeat analysis, while follow-up measurements confirm further predictions. This would test whether the explanation survives scrutiny.

milestones.label: Particle abundance fits galactic dark matter
milestones.explanation: The interpretation would have to fit independent galactic density estimates and quantify how abundance trades off against interaction strength. This would test cosmic consistency without proving the species supplies all dark matter.

milestones.label: The identification has clearly stated boundaries
milestones.explanation: The claim would have to specify tested masses, interactions, detector conditions and assumptions about the Galaxy. These boundaries would define what the identification establishes and which questions remain open.

uncertain: A detected species could supply some or all dark matter; identification alone would not settle its share.
The relevant interaction could be weaker than these searches can detect, or the constituent could differ from the candidates they test.
The proposed discovery benchmarks are not an established consensus standard.

page.title: Laboratory identification of a dark-matter constituent
page.definition: Independent laboratory measurements identify a particle or field in the Milky Way’s dark matter and constrain its mass and interaction strength. A weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) can scatter from an atomic nucleus, causing it to recoil. A microwave-cavity haloscope searches for photons produced when Galactic axions pass through a strong magnetic field.

goal.need: In the standard cosmological model, cold dark matter outweighs ordinary matter by a factor of about 5.36. Its gravity shapes galaxies, yet several particle models fit the gravitational evidence. A direct measurement would let physicists test how one constituent interacts with ordinary matter and use its measured properties in models of galaxy formation. Inferring the interaction strength from the signal rate depends on how much of that constituent is present near the Sun.

completion.title: A laboratory dark-matter discovery is independently confirmed as a Galactic constituent.
completion.criterion: A laboratory excess reaches 5σ global significance and is reproduced by a second independent experiment. Both signals support a common Galactic dark-matter constituent, with controlled backgrounds and a viable mass and interaction model consistent with other laboratory, astrophysical and cosmological constraints. For scattering, confirmation uses a second target. Mass and interaction constraints retain their local-abundance assumptions; identification need not establish that the constituent supplies all dark matter.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of published discovery and confirmation criteria. No cited body specifies the full test for both WIMP and axion searches.
completion.threshold_quote: replication is an option of last resort to fully confirm or rule out any potential signal for dark matter.
completion.basis: The Particle Data Group describes the 5σ particle-physics convention and the correction for searching multiple signal hypotheses. Snowmass CF1 discusses replication in section 4.3.5. For WIMP scattering, APPEC section 4.7 calls for a second target, and the Dark Matter Scientific Assessment Group describes how recoil spectra and rates should vary across targets. For resonant axion searches, APPEC section 5.2 describes independent instruments tuned to the candidate frequency. Essig’s checks address backgrounds and consistency with other probes.

milestones.title: A laboratory search recovers a blinded synthetic dark-matter signal.
milestones.criterion: Apply the search analysis while the injections are hidden from the analysts. In the ADMX protocol, flag the injected radio signal as a candidate and verify on rescan that it disappears with the generator off. In the LZ protocol, fix the event selection and likelihood models before revealing the injected WIMP-like events, then compare their survival through selection with the expected signal efficiency.
milestones.set_by: ADMX Collaboration’s published synthetic-axion protocol, written for axion searches; LZ Collaboration’s published salting procedure supplies the corresponding WIMP-search demonstration.
milestones.threshold_quote: the region is rescanned with the signal turned off, and the signal is verified as having disappeared.

milestones.title: A laboratory dark-matter excess reaches 3σ global significance.
milestones.criterion: For a Galactic dark-matter signal hypothesis, obtain a global significance of at least 3σ against the background-only hypothesis. This corresponds to a one-sided p-value of approximately 1.35 × 10⁻³ or smaller after accounting for the signal hypotheses searched, including candidate masses or frequencies.
milestones.set_by: Baxter et al., direct-detection community recommendations, sections 2.1.1 and 4.1. Formulated primarily for weak-scale searches; the authors explicitly discuss broader application, including axions.
milestones.threshold_quote: Claims of evidence should require at least a $3\sigma$ global discrepancy with the background-only hypothesis.

milestones.title: A laboratory dark-matter search rejects background at 5σ global significance.
milestones.criterion: Test a Galactic dark-matter signal against the background-only hypothesis, accounting for uncertainties in the background and detector response and for the range of signal hypotheses searched. The excess must reach a global significance of at least 5σ, corresponding to a one-sided p-value of approximately 2.87 × 10⁻⁷ or smaller.
milestones.set_by: Particle Data Group, 2025 Statistics review, sections 40.3.2 and 40.3.2.2; the conventional particle-physics discovery threshold, with correction for searches over signal hypotheses.
milestones.threshold_quote: a 5σ effect, corresponding to a p-value of 2.87 × 10−7.

milestones.title: A laboratory search sets a 90% confidence upper limit on interaction strength at a stated mass.
milestones.criterion: Use search data to report a 90% confidence upper limit on the WIMP scattering cross section or the magnitude of the axion–photon coupling at a specified mass. State the interaction model and the assumed local density and velocity distribution of the candidate. The limit must use observed data rather than projected sensitivity.
milestones.set_by: Baxter et al., direct-detection reporting recommendations, section 4.1. LZ applies the convention to WIMP scattering and ADMX to axion–photon conversion.
milestones.threshold_quote: the primary limit should use $\alpha=0.1$ (i.e. 90% CL).

not_found: No universal numerical mass- or coupling-precision requirement for constituent identification was found in P5, APPEC, Snowmass CF1, PDG or the direct-detection consensus recommendations.

results.finding: ADMX recovered 100% of blinded axion injections and verified their disappearance on generator-off rescans. The injection count was unreported.
results.quote:
All the synthetic signals were identified suc-
cessfully and excluded with rescans when the SAG was
turned off during our data taking.

results.finding: ADMX set 90% confidence upper limits on axion–photon coupling at 3.27–3.34 μeV using its 71-day 2022 run and earlier data.
results.detail: The paper also reports limits for an N-body velocity distribution with a local density of 0.63 GeV/cm³.
results.quote:
In summary, we set the most sensitive exclusion limits of
gaγγ with 90% CL as a function of the axion mass between
3.27 and 3.34 μeV (Fig. 4), excluding the DFSZ axion as
the dominant local dark matter with such masses with the
same CL.

results.finding: ADMX found local 3σ excesses in 1 Maxwell–Boltzmann and 11 N-body candidate bins after combining runs. All failed persistence checks.
results.detail: The counts are for two signal templates and need not represent distinct frequencies. A local 3σ flag does not establish the required global 3σ significance.
results.quote:
All the 3σ excesses for both scenarios fail the
persistence check as described below.

results.finding: COSINE-100 and ANAIS-112 recovered synthetic annual modulation with negligible mean bias across about 10,000 pseudo-experiments per ensemble.
results.detail: The simulations included eight nonzero modulation amplitudes and one zero-amplitude control.
results.quote: Approximately 10,000 pseudo-experiments were generated per ensemble to quantify potential biases, defined as the difference between the injected signal and the fit result. For all ensembles, mean biases were found to be negligible.

results.finding: CDMSlite Run 3 retained 105 of 393 blinded WIMP-like injections in the signal region.
results.detail: The reported 26% compares the surviving injections with the 401 surviving real events. It does not measure signal efficiency.
results.quote:
Upon unblinding, the number of
salt events was revealed to be 393. After application of
the selection cuts described in Sec. IV and V the number
of salt events in the signal region was reduced to 105,
which constituted 26% of the number of true events that
survived selection cuts in the signal region (401 events).

results.finding: CDMSlite Run 3 (401 events, 36 kg-days) set a 90% confidence upper limit of 5.4 × 10⁻⁴² cm² on spin-independent WIMP–nucleon scattering at 5 GeV/c².
results.quote:
This
analysis sets an upper limit on the dark matter-nucleon
scattering cross section in germanium of 5.4 ×10−42 cm2
at 5 GeV/c2, which is a factor of∼2.5 improvement over
the previous CDMSlite result.

results.finding: ADMX confirmed 8 blinded synthetic axion signals among 10 persistent candidates on the generator-off rescan.
results.detail: The TM 011 mode scan identified one additional blinded injection. An ambient check identified the remaining candidate as radio-frequency interference.
results.quote:
Eight were confirmed as
blind signals injected by the SAG system after the second
rescan.

results.finding: One ADMX search run over 4.54–5.41 μeV set 90% confidence upper limits on the axion–photon coupling.
results.detail: Figure 3 gives the coupling values by mass. Cavity-mode crossings leave gaps in the limit curve.
results.quote:
From this
analysis we can compute the exclusion limit for gaγγ at 90%
CL as a function of frequency assuming a local dark matter
density of 0.45 GeV=cm3 for the Maxwell-Boltzmann
model.

results.finding: PICO-60 (2571 kg·days) set a 90% confidence upper limit of 3.2 × 10⁻⁴¹ cm² on spin-dependent WIMP–proton scattering at 25 GeV/c².
results.quote:
These results set the most stringent direct-detection constraint
to date on the weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP)-proton spin-dependent cross section at
3.2 × 10−41 cm2 for a 25 GeV WIMP, improving on previous PICO results for 3–5 GeV WIMPs by
an order of magnitude.

results.finding: CAPP-12TB scanned 1,996 resonant frequencies and set a 90% axion–photon coupling upper limit of about 6.2 × 10⁻¹⁶ GeV⁻¹ across the covered portions of 4.51–4.59 μeV.
results.detail: A 380 kHz gap from cavity mode crossings interrupts coverage near 4.527 μeV.
results.quote:
The search excluded
the axion-photon coupling gaγγ down to about 6.2 × 10−16 GeV−1 over the axion mass range between 4.51
and 4.59 μeV at a 90% confidence level.

definition = "Independent laboratory measurements identify a particle or field in the Milky Way\u2019s dark matter and constrain its mass and interaction strength. A weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) can scatter from an atomic nucleus, causing it to recoil. A microwave-cavity haloscope searches for photons produced when Galactic axions pass through a strong magnetic field.". Reason: The definition names two candidates but explains the observable for only one of them.

goal.need = "In the standard cosmological model, cold dark matter outweighs ordinary matter by a factor of about 5.36. Its gravity shapes galaxies, yet several particle models fit the gravitational evidence. A direct measurement would let physicists test how one constituent interacts with ordinary matter and use its measured properties in models of galaxy formation. Inferring the interaction strength from the signal rate depends on how much of that constituent is present near the Sun.". Reason: The current text points to density parameters that readers cannot see and omits both the use in galaxy-formation models and the dependence on local abundance.

edit completion: set_by = "Atlas synthesis of published discovery and confirmation criteria. No cited body specifies the full test for both WIMP and axion searches."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; basis = "The Particle Data Group describes the 5\u03c3 particle-physics convention and the correction for searching multiple signal hypotheses. Snowmass CF1 discusses replication in section 4.3.5. For WIMP scattering, APPEC section 4.7 calls for a second target, and the Dark Matter Scientific Assessment Group describes how recoil spectra and rates should vary across targets. For resonant axion searches, APPEC section 5.2 describes independent instruments tuned to the candidate frequency. Essig\u2019s checks address backgrounds and consistency with other probes."; refs = [6, 4, 3, 20, 5]. Reason: The attribution gives the wrong Snowmass section and presents a combined test as though a single community convention prescribed all its conditions.

edit m1: criterion = "Apply the search analysis while the injections are hidden from the analysts. In the ADMX protocol, flag the injected radio signal as a candidate and verify on rescan that it disappears with the generator off. In the LZ protocol, fix the event selection and likelihood models before revealing the injected WIMP-like events, then compare their survival through selection with the expected signal efficiency.". Reason: The criterion mixes run results with the test and leaves unclear how LZ can verify recovery while keeping the identities of injected events hidden.

add milestone after m1: "A laboratory search sets a 90% confidence upper limit on interaction strength at a stated mass.". Reason: A measured upper limit is a distinct laboratory result between recovering an artificial signal and observing evidence for a Galactic signal.

This corresponds to a one-sided p-value of approximately 1.35 \u00d7 10\u207b\u00b3 or smaller after accounting for the signal hypotheses searched, including candidate masses or frequencies."; threshold_quote = "Claims of evidence should require at least a $3\\sigma$ global discrepancy with the background-only hypothesis."; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10]. Reason: The revision aligns the evidence threshold with the cited recommendation’s inclusive wording and removes experimental results from the criterion.
